text: Git branching is a powerful tool in version control that helps teams work on code without interfering with each other. When starting a new task, developers create a *feature branch* from the main codebase. This branch is a separate copy where they can try new ideas safely. Once the work is finished, they can *merge* that branch back into the main line. This process is often managed through a *pull request*, which allows other teammates to review the changes before they become permanent. The main branches usually protect the stable version of the software. This *version control workflow* keeps the project organized, reduces conflicts, and makes it easy to track what was changed and why. Understanding branching is essential for smooth collaboration in any software project.
